resources.string: No Hosts yet. Add one below.
Aries needs an SSH key to sign in to your Hosts.
Add it to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on each Host.
QR code of this phone\'s SSH public key
Sign in once with the password for %1$s. Aries adds this phone\'s public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys and uses only the key after that. The password is not saved.
This phone\'s key was added on %1$s. Aries now connects with the key.
%1$s already had this phone\'s key. Nothing was changed.
The Host did not accept the user name or password. The Host may also have password login turned off; then add the public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys by hand.
Signed in, but could not write ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the Host: %1$s\n\nCheck that the user owns ~/.ssh and can write to it.
Aries forgets this Host\'s address, its trusted Host key and everything stored for it on this phone. Nothing on the Host itself changes.
No Terminals are running on this Host.
herdr-app has not saved a layout on this Host. Terminals are grouped by their Space and Tab labels.
The herdr-app layout on this Host could not be read (%1$s). Terminals are grouped by their Space and Tab labels.
The herdr-app layout on this Host is in a format Aries does not know. Terminals are grouped by their Space and Tab labels. Update Aries.
The connection to the Host closed. What you see may be out of date.

This is the first connection to %1$s. Check that its Host key fingerprint is:

%2$s

On the Host, run: ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub

The Host presented a different key than before, so Aries did not connect. Someone may be intercepting the connection, or the Host was reinstalled.

Trusted: %1$s
Now: %2$s
This Host runs a newer herdr-core protocol (generation %1$d). Update Aries.
This Host runs herdr-core %1$s. Aries needs %2$s or newer: run `hc update` on the Host.
This Host\'s herdr-core lacks %1$s. Run `hc update` on the Host.
The Host did not accept this phone\'s SSH key. Add the public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the Host.
The Host did not speak the herdr-core protocol: %1$s
The Beacon can only be installed on an SSH Host.
Could not read the Beacon on this Host.
The Beacon is not installed. It sends notifications and Calls from this Host.
The Beacon service is not running.
Running, not attached to herdr-core yet.
This app does not support Beacon %1$s (it needs %2$s). Reinstall the Beacon.
The Beacon only runs while you are logged in to the Host. To keep it running, run on the Host: sudo loginctl enable-linger %1$s
Beacon stops when you log out

The Beacon is installed, but the Host refused to keep your services running after logout (%1$s). Without that the Beacon, and its notifications, stop until you log in again.\n\nOn the Host, run: sudo loginctl enable-linger %2$s
This stops the Beacon on %1$s and removes its service and program. Call history stays on the Host.

The downloaded Beacon does not match the checksum built into this app, so nothing was installed.

Expected: %1$s
Got: %2$s
The Beacon does not support %1$s/%2$s Hosts.
This version of Aries has no Beacon for %1$s/%2$s yet.
The Beacon needs an update (%1$s to %2$s). Automatic updates are off, so nothing was installed.
Beacon runs only while you are logged in

The Beacon is installed as a macOS LaunchAgent. macOS ties LaunchAgents to your login session: the Beacon, and its notifications, stop when you log out of the Mac and start again at your next login, also after a restart.
On macOS the Beacon runs only while you are logged in to the Mac.
Aries signs in to each jump host in order, then to the Host through the last one.
No jump hosts: Aries connects to the Host directly.

This is the first connection to jump host %1$d (%2$s) on the way to %3$s. Check that its Host key fingerprint is:

%4$s

On the jump host, run: ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub

Jump host %1$d (%2$s) presented a different key than before, so Aries did not connect. Someone may be intercepting the connection, or the jump host was reinstalled.

Trusted: %3$s
Now: %4$s
Jump host %1$d (%2$s) did not accept the key chosen for it. Add that key\'s public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the jump host.
